body:
Danielle Levy News, Top 3 Bank of England, Barclays, private credit

The Bank of England is understood to be reviewing whether Barclays’ traders misrepresented private credit loans to understate their risk.

The investigation follows a complaint by an insider earlier this year about how the bank was recording derivatives used to finance the loans it issues to private credit firms, according to the Financial Times.

The review centres on whether Barclays logged the total return swaps in the trading book rather than the banking book, indicating they carried less risk and therefore required less capital to be set aside to cover potential losses.

If this was the case, it would have reduced capital requirements and may have provided a boost to profitability.

According to Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) rules, banks are unable to assign derivatives backed by illiquid collateral to their trading book unless they can provide evidence to prove otherwise.

Barclays was approached for comment at the time of writing.
